title: Packages
description: Learn about package declaration, importing, exporting, and init functions in Go
theory:
## Packages in Go

In this course, put multiple files in **one editor buffer**: use **`// File: path/to/file.go`** before each file, or a line with only **`---`** between files. Press **`r`** to build module **`learnsnippet`** and run **`go run .`**. Import your packages as **`learnsnippet/utils`**, **`learnsnippet/counter`**, etc.

Packages are the way Go organizes code. Every Go file belongs to a package.

### Package Declaration

```go
package main  // executable package
package utils // library package
```

### The main Package

- `package main` is special - it tells Go this will compile to an executable
- Must have a main() function as entry point

### Importing Packages

```go
import (
    "fmt"         // standard library
    "math"       // standard library
    "yourmodule/utils"  // your own package
)
```

### Exported Names

- Only names starting with **uppercase** are exported (visible to other packages)
- `func MyFunc()` is exported
- `func myFunc()` is not exported

### Package Initialization

```go
var config map[string]string

func init() {
    config = make(map[string]string)
    config["key"] = "value"
}
```

- `init()` runs automatically before main() when the package is first imported
- Only one init() per package
- Useful for setup/initialization

### Package Naming Convention

- Use short, descriptive names
- `fmt` instead of `formatting`
- But not too short: `buf` (buffer) is OK
- Usually match the directory name

### go.mod and Module

```go
module example.com/myapp

go 1.21
```

- go.mod defines your module
- Import path matches module name

exercises.title: Package Declaration
exercises.description: In one buffer: `main.go` imports `learnsnippet/utils`; `utils/utils.go` defines `Greet()`. Press **`r`** to run the module.
hints: Use // File: path lines or a --- line between files in the editor
Import learnsnippet/utils from main; package name in utils/utils.go is utils

exercises.title: Importing Standard Library
exercises.description: Import the math package and use math.Sqrt to calculate the square root of 144. Print the result.
exercises.starter_code:
package main

// Import math package and print square root of 144
hints: Use import "math" to import the math package
Use fmt.Println to print the result

exercises.title: Exporting Names
exercises.description: In one buffer: `// File: main.go` imports `learnsnippet/counter`; `// File: counter/counter.go` exports `Count` and `Increment`. Print count before and after increment.
hints: Export by capitalizing: Count, Increment (Go exports anything starting with uppercase)
In main, use counter.Count and counter.Increment()

exercises.title: Init Functions
hints: Declare var Version string in config package
Define func init() that assigns "1.0.0" to Version
init() runs automatically before main() when the package is imported

exercises.title: Unexported Names
exercises.description: Two files: `formatter/formatter.go` has `Format` (exported) and `format` (unexported); `main.go` calls only `Format`.
hints: Define func Format() and func format() in formatter package
Only Format is accessible from main

exercises.title: Import Alias
exercises.description: Import the fmt package with the alias io, then use io.Println to print "Hello".
hints: Use import io "fmt" to create an alias

exercises.title: Multiple Imports
exercises.description: Import both fmt and strings packages. Use fmt.Println with strings.ToUpper to print "hello" in uppercase.
